facts.statement: Songzia was an extinct genus of birds related to rails.
facts.quote: Songzia is an extinct genus of gruiform bird related to rails.

facts.statement: Fossils of Songzia have been found in Songzi county, Hubei Province, China.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in Songzi county (Hubei Province People's Republic of China).

facts.statement: Two species of Songzia are known: Songzia heidangkouensis and Songzia acutunguis.
facts.quote: Two species are known and have been named Songzia heidangkouensis and Songzia acutunguis.

facts.statement: The names for the genus and family were originally published in a newsletter before being validated in a scientific journal.
facts.quote: The genus and family names for the type species were originally first published in a newsletter, and only subsequently in a scientific journal to fulfill the ICZN's requirements valid new scientific names.

facts.statement: Songzia lived during the Eocene epoch.
facts.quote: It lived in the Eocene epoch.

facts.statement: Songzia lived between 56 and 48.07 million years ago during the Ypresian age.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 48.07 million years ago)

facts.statement: Songzia belongs to the family Songziidae.
Fossils from the Driftwood site in the Eocene Okanagan Highlands and the Paleocene Menat Formation have been tentatively assigned to the family Songziidae.
facts.quote: An additional fossil found in the Driftwood site avifauna of the Eocene Okanagan Highlands was tentatively referred the to family, as has a fossil from the Paleocene Menat Formation

rejected.statement: Songzia is classified in the class Aves.
